script: In 1940, one man volunteered to be captured and sent into Auschwitz, on purpose. His name was Witold Pilecki, a Polish cavalry officer who believed the world needed hard proof of what the Nazis were building. He deliberately walked into a German street roundup in occupied Warsaw and quietly let himself be arrested. Inside the camp, he built a secret resistance network of hundreds of starving prisoners, right under the noses of the guards. His reports were smuggled out in laundry carts and reached London itself, the first eyewitness accounts of the camp the Allies ever read. But here is the part that truly breaks your heart, the Allies did not believe the scale of what he described. After two and a half brutal years inside, he escaped through a bakery door at night and kept on fighting. He survived the entire war, only to be executed by the communist government he had also dared to resist. Poland then erased his name from its history books for forty long years, until the archives finally opened. The man who volunteered into hell to warn the world was silenced by it, twice.
